answer: Coordinated Action Tax. Every agent action carries a fee set by how many distinct identities act within a short window; each additional identity in the window raises the fee for all. An attacker spawning many agents pays steeply rising marginal costs per action, while a single agent doing varied work pays little. Fees accrue as an ember held against future fees. Identity metadata commits to a velvet hash chain linking registrations. The operator publishes a marble audit log of window counts, making the tax publicly checkable.
